# bugs #3153: Multiple definition of line symbols at link time with --debug for static functions defined in a header

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3153/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17200
- Recommended action: Choose between this sdld patch and module names in the line symbols, which change the CDB format. The patch does not have a test.
- Patch: [bugs-3153.patch](../../patches/bugs-3153.patch), commit [`91bbbce22`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/91bbbce222cfca052daf8531cedfa21e81ca2c27). Applies to r17200 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The ticket's case is a function that a header defines `inline` without `static`.
[r12010](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/12010/) fixed it by omitting the line symbols of
code that the compiler expands inline. The case that the thirteenth and the sixteenth comment
leave open fails. When the function is `static inline`, or `static` without `inline`, and more
than one source file includes the header, the linker reports
`?ASlink-Error-Multiple definition of C$inline.h$16$1_0$2` and the same error for the other lines
of the function.

The test program has the ticket's files and a definition of the array, which the attachment does
not have. Three source files include the header. On r17193 with the earlier patches of this
report, the link of both `static` forms fails for the six mcs51 variants, z80, and stm8.

## Cause

`cdbWriteCLine` in `src/cdbFile.c` names the symbol for each line of C code
`C$file$line$level$block`, from the base name of the source file, the line, the level, and the
block number. The name does not have the module name, and the `emitDebuggerSymbol` function of
each port defines the symbol as a global symbol. `createFunction` in `src/SDCCast.c` generates
code for every `static inline` function, so each module that includes the header defines the
symbols of the function's lines. The names are equal when the function has the same block number
in each module, and `newsym` in `sdas/linksrc/lksym.c` reports the second definition. When the
block numbers differ, the link succeeds, which is the effect in the ninth comment.

## Fix

When a name that begins with `C$` already has a definition, `newsym` creates another symbol entry
for the new definition and does not report an error. The change is inside `#if SDCDB`. The
compiler is not changed, and it writes names with this prefix only for lines, in `cdbWriteCLine`
and `cdbWriteEndFunction`.

With the patch, the map file and the `.cdb` file have one record with the name for each module
that has code for the line. For line 16 of the header, the `.cdb` file of the mcs51 small model
has `L:C$inline.h$16$1_0$2:A9`, `L:C$inline.h$16$1_0$2:CE`, and `L:C$inline.h$16$1_0$2:F7`.

## Decision

The patch makes the linker accept equal names and keeps the CDB format. The alternative adds the
module name to the line symbols in `src/cdbFile.c`. That changes the record
`L:C$file$line$level$block:address`, and it needs changes in `lnkCSrc` in
`debugger/mcs51/symtab.c`, in `sdas/linksrc/lkaomf51.c`, and in programs outside SDCC that read
`.cdb` files. It was not written. The patch has these costs:

- By the code, sdld accepts a second definition of every global symbol whose name begins with
  `C$`, including symbols that hand-written assembly defines. It reports a second definition of
  every other name, and two modules that define one variable get "Multiple definition of _x" with
  the patch.
- Programs that read the `.cdb` file get several records with one name. Without the patch they
  get several records for one line of a header when the block numbers differ, such as
  `L:C$inline.h$16$1_0$2:B0` and `L:C$inline.h$16$1_0$5:DA` on r17193. `lnkCSrc` takes the
  address of the last record for a line, and with the patch sdcdb set the breakpoint for
  `inline.h:16` at that address. By the code, `lkaomf51.c` keeps the first address of a line, and
  only for source files whose base name is a module name.
- sdldz80, sdldgb, sdldstm8, sdld6808, sdldpdk, and sdldf8 are copies of sdld. The patch was
  tested for mcs51, z80, and stm8. sdldgb, the linker of the ticket, was not run.

## Verification

The patch does not have a test in the tree, because the regression suite links one module per
test and does not pass `--debug`. The test program was linked with the header function as
`inline`, as `static inline`, and as `static`, for the six mcs51 variants, z80, and stm8. With the
patch the 24 links succeed. For the mcs51 small and large models, the link also succeeds with two
of the modules in a library made with sdar.

With the series of this report up to the patch for #4159 applied to r17193, the regression suite
has 0 failures for host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80.

## Related

- In the thirteenth comment a maintainer describes a second problem. Within one module the
  compiler writes the symbol of a line more than once when the code of the line is not
  contiguous, and the assembler keeps the last definition. The patch does not change this.
- In the fourth comment the reporter names bug #2591 as similar. That ticket is closed.
